answer: Anchor every agent identity to a small refundable stake held in escrow, and let reputation grow on a trellis of mutual attestations: peers vouch only after real work together, and each vouch is signed and capped. A lone agent cannot cheaply spin up a hundred fakes, because each fake needs its own stake and its own history of earned trust, while honest agents wander freely between services carrying their record with them. If one identity misbehaves, its stake is slashed and every attestation it gave is flagged, so the cost of an attack scales with each fake rather than staying flat.
